name: One-Arm Barbell Row
description: A unilateral back exercise using a barbell loaded on one end (the other end is anchored in a landmine or wedged into a corner). The single-arm pulling pattern allows greater range of motion than many cable or dumbbell rows and loads the lat, rhomboid, and rear deltoid through a unique diagonal force vector.

execution.starting_position: Straddle the barbell end with one foot forward. Hinge at the hips and grip the loaded end of the barbell with the outside hand.
execution.setup_instructions: Anchor a barbell in a landmine attachment or corner. Load the free end. Stand beside the weighted end in a staggered stance.
steps: Step 1: Hinge at the hips to approximately 45 degrees with the core braced.
Step 2: Pull the loaded end of the bar up toward the hip, driving the elbow back and out.
Step 3: At the top, rotate the shoulder slightly to increase lat contraction.
Step 4: Lower under control to full arm extension and repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso excessively to assist the pull
safety_considerations: This row allows the shoulder to pronate at the top for increased range — this is intentional
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the bottom. Bar pulled to the hip at the top.
coaching_cues: Drive the elbow back and out
